page: Microsoft Azure E96-24s_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the ESv5 server family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The server features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz, configured with 12 physical cores and 24 vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 672.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 28.0 GB per vCPU. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, but it is Premium Storage capable for remote disk attachments.

In benchmark testing, the E96-24s_v5 demonstrates strong memory performance, scoring in the top 25% for both the Passmark memory score and large-block memory write bandwidth at 106.74 GB/sec. Its single-core and multi-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng and Geekbench, falls within the average range. The instance also shows strong capabilities in text generation for small language models, achieving 263.29 tokens per second, while medium and large model inference speeds remain in the average tier.

This server configuration offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that do not scale linearly with CPU core counts. By providing 672.0 GB of RAM alongside a moderate allocation of 24 vCPUs, it reduces licensing and compute overhead for large in-memory databases, caching layers, and enterprise resource planning systems. It is well-suited for memory-bound applications, large-scale Redis deployments, and data analytics pipelines requiring massive memory footprints without requiring high-density CPU parallelization.
